claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a lamellar eutectic high-entropy alloy containing L12 and B2 phases.
The L12 phase is CoCrFe-rich and the B2 phase is AlNi-rich.
A hybrid route consisting of cryo-rolling followed by warm-rolling at approximately 600 °C can be applied to AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The cryo-rolling stage itself should impose a true strain of approximately 2.4, corresponding to about 90% thickness reduction, before warm-rolling.
The cited hybrid-rolling schedule uses approximately 1.2 strain in each of the cryo-rolling and warm-rolling stages, for a total strain of approximately 2.4 and 90% thickness reduction.
Strain increments of approximately 1.2 should be imposed per rolling pass.
Processing under an inert atmosphere is required for the proposed benefits.
A post-rolling anneal near 700 °C for 30–50 seconds will promote the desired microstructure.
Hybrid rolling produces a heterogeneous microstructure containing retained lamellar regions and transformed nanocrystalline regions.
The nanocrystalline regions form specifically as interfacial layers at lamellar colony boundaries embedded within coarse lamellae.
Preferential deformation during cryo-rolling creates high stored energy in boundary or disrupted lamellar regions, which drives transformations during subsequent warm-rolling.
Warm-rolling followed by the proposed short anneal causes localized partial recrystallization at internal colony boundaries.
Nanocrystalline interfacial layers deflect or arrest propagating microcracks.
Retained coarse lamellae preserve ductility and deform by twinning, thereby enhancing strain hardening.
Hybrid-rolled AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can exhibit a high combined strength and ductility of approximately 2000 MPa and 8%, respectively.
Relative to the unmodified lamellar baseline, the proposed treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 20–30% and room-temperature tensile ductility by approximately 50%.
The treatment will increase the work-hardening rate and reduce microcrack nucleation at internal boundaries.
Unmodified AlCoCrFeNi2.1 exhibits a strength–ductility trade-off and preferential microcrack initiation at lamellar colony boundaries.
Excessive annealing will cause over-recrystallization or coarsening that removes the proposed ductility benefit.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and intervention assign approximately 2.4 true strain and 90% reduction to the initial cryo-rolling stage, whereas the conditions imply approximately 1.2 strain increments and the cited process assigns 1.2 to each of two stages for a total of 2.4. The intended strain allocation is therefore internally ambiguous.
